question: For what share of people with low back pain can a doctor name a specific cause?
answer: Only about one in ten. The remaining 90% or so is labelled non-specific: no fracture, infection, tumour or trapped nerve explains it. This is the condition that causes more years lived with disability worldwide than any other. Most of that burden rests on a diagnosis that says what the pain is not.
move: A common label can mean nobody knows yet.
ask: Which confident label in my life really just means nobody knows the cause yet?
